newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - May 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Traders say some shares which have not been subject to corrections still have to go through them as they do not reflect the real value of their companies.

- Spanish operators attending seminar on EU partnership on fisheries industries insisted on the need to ease legal framework for the setting up of joint ventures. But these firms are less likely to be created as concern to preserve resources grows.

- Casablanca-based pharmaceutical subsidiaries respectively of German Hoeschst and French Roussel Uclaf will announce in July merger into one company. The new firm, called Hoechst Marion Roussel, plans to increase its turnover to 900 million dirhams ($95.8 million) from the current 500 million in four years.
- Corrections on Casablanca Stock Exchange are making stocks more attractive for potential buyers. Prices are pulled down by small shareholders and mutual funds.

- Mobil oil Morocco has been investing 50 million dirhams ($5.3 million) annually since 1994 to revamp filling stations and train its staff. Managing director James MacDonald says there is need to increase margins on fuel sales to ensure returns on investments.

- Fisheries, Merchant Navy Minister Mustapha Sahel says he is against renewal of fish accord with EU and proposes instead to attract investors in order to develop Morocco's processing industries. He says Morocco wants to stabilise fish stocks and buy new fishing vessels.
